ingredients.name: cayenne pepper or hot sauce, optional
butter, for spreading on the muffins, optional

steps.instruction: Blend 3 egg yolks and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice in a blender.
steps.spoken: Blend the egg yolks and lemon juice in a blender. This is the base of the hollandaise sauce. You can also whisk them in a double boiler on a gentle simmer instead, which helps keep the sauce from curdling.

steps.instruction: Slowly pour in 1/2 cup of melted butter while blending.
steps.spoken: Slowly pour in the melted butter while blending. The sauce should thicken and become creamy. If it gets too thick, add a little warm water or lemon juice.

steps.instruction: Season the sauce with cayenne pepper or hot sauce, to taste.
Bring 4 inches of water in a large saucepan to a gentle simmer.
Add 1 tablespoon of white vinegar to the water.
steps.spoken: Add the vinegar to the water. It helps the egg whites set.

steps.instruction: Slide 4 eggs gently into the simmering water.
steps.spoken: Gently slide the eggs into the water. It helps to crack each egg into a small bowl or ladle first, bring it to the surface of the water, and let the egg slide in. Stir the water into a little whirlpool while the eggs cook. Cook for 3 to four minutes.

steps.instruction: Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Split 2 english muffins and toast them.
Butter both halves of the muffins if you like.
steps.spoken: Butter both halves if you like. You can use any kind of spongy bread instead of the muffins.

steps.instruction: Cook 4 slices of Canadian bacon in a skillet over medium heat until slightly browned.
Put a slice of bacon on each muffin half and top with an egg and hollandaise sauce.
Garnish with chopped chives and more cayenne pepper if you like.
